entries.title: Transport, Entropy, and the Cost of Dependence: Maximum Conditional Entropy under Transport Constraints
entries.summary: Maximum-entropy inference under Wasserstein constraints can be computationally challenging due to the underlying optimization over transport couplings. We investigate a tractable alternative based on maximizing conditional entropy under an average transport constraint. On Euclidean spaces, this formulation admits an explicit generalized-Gaussian additive-noise solution, providing a feasible approximation to the Wasserstein-constrained problem without solving an optimal transport problem. We establish quantitative bounds on the resulting optimality gap by showing that the two formulations admit a common feasible-marginal representation, with their discrepancy characterized by the mutual information retained between the nominal and perturbed variables. For discretely supported nominal distributions, we further obtain an exact decomposition of the gap into a marginal-entropy gain and a weighted Jensen-Shannon divergence.

entries.title: Quantitative Gaussian limits of periodic O(N) models at and below the critical temperature
entries.summary: We prove a volume-uniform Gaussian approximation for local spin coordinates in the zero-field nearest-neighbour $O(N)$ model on periodic boxes of side $M$ in $d\ge3$, at and below the critical temperature of the limiting spherical model. On a fixed spatial window, for sufficiently large $M,N$, the unnormalized $1$-Wasserstein error for the first $p\le N$ coordinates is at most $C\sqrt p (N^{-1/2}+s_M)$, where $s_M\to0$ is the spectral shift of the finite-volume mean spherical model. The estimate is uniform on compact ranges of positive directional couplings and inverse temperatures. The target has independent coordinate fields, each a scaled anisotropic Gaussian free field with an independent spatially constant Gaussian term below criticality. On a window containing a nearest-neighbour star (a site and its $d$ positive-direction neighbours), the error tends to zero as $M,N\to\infty$ exactly when $p=o(N)$ and $\sqrt p s_M\to0$. For any choice of periodic infinite-volume accumulation states, the error on any nonempty fixed window tends to zero as $N\to\infty$ exactly when $p=o(N)$. In $d\ge5$, when the inverse temperature exceeds its critical value by at least a fixed positive amount, the bound improves to $C(p/N+\sqrt p M^{-d})$. For fixed $p$, the sharp order is $N^{-1}+M^{-d}$ on star-containing windows and $N^{-1}$ on every nonempty fixed window in periodic accumulation states.

entries.title: Stylization as Geodesic Navigation on Diffusion Manifolds
entries.summary: Facial stylization asks for a delicate transformation: the image should look unmistakably artistic, yet the person should remain unmistakably the same. Existing training-free and instruction-driven methods often fail to expose such control, either drifting away from identity or producing only weak stylization. We introduce Stylus, a training-free framework that treats facial style transfer as navigation on the curved latent manifold of a pretrained diffusion model. Rather than interpolating in flat Euclidean space, \method refines the interpolated content--style point by lowering a ratio-weighted discrete geodesic energy under the pullback metric, made tractable by a rank-one power-iteration approximation of the Jacobian. This principle drives two complementary controls: content--style latent interpolation for smooth semantic fusion, and self-attention query optimization for spatially adaptive style injection. The resulting dual-control mechanism provides continuous, fine-grained control over stylization strength while preserving identity-critical facial structure, all without additional training. Experiments show that Stylus achieves the strongest identity and content preservation at competitive stylization strength.

entries.title: Quantitative stability of classical, entropic, and doubly entropic Wasserstein barycenters
entries.summary: In this paper, we show how the recent analysis of (sharp) strong convexity properties of the Kantorovich functional by the third author can be used to establish new global quantitative stability estimates for Wasserstein barycenters and their entropic regularizations with respect to perturbations of the population distribution. For classical Wasserstein barycenters, we improve the state-of-the-art Hölder continuity exponent with respect to the $\mathcal{W}_1$ metric from $1/6$ to $1/4$, while drastically weakening the assumptions on the population distribution. We also provide an example which shows that the exponent $1/4$ cannot be improved. Motivated by computational considerations, we also analyze regularizations of Wasserstein barycenters with \emph{outer} and \emph{inner} entropic penalizations. For outer entropic barycenters, we establish novel higher-order stability results and in particular give a quantitative bound on relative Fisher information. Another contribution of our paper is a strong convexity estimate for an entropic version of the Kantorovich functional via soft Legendre transforms, enabling us to extend our stability results to \emph{doubly} entropic barycenters, as introduced by Chizat.

entries.title: Mean-field BSDEs with jumps under quadratic-exponential growth
entries.summary: This paper studies the well-posedness of mean-field backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs, for short) with Poisson jumps, where the generator has quadratic growth with respect to $Z$ and exponential growth with respect to $U$, where $(Y,Z,U)$ denotes the solution of this BSDE. First, we prove the existence and the uniqueness of local solutions to mean-field backward stochastic differential equations with jumps (BSDEJs, for short) by using a fixed-point argument. Then, based on these local results, we discuss the solvability of global solutions in the following two cases: in the first one, the generator has linear growth with respect to $Y$ and the corresponding marginal distribution $μ_1$; and in the second one, the generator has subquadratic growth with respect to the marginal distribution $μ_2$ and linear growth with respect to the marginal distribution $μ_3$, corresponding to $Z$ and $U$, respectively. Finally, by employing a Girsanov transformation we establish a comparison theorem for mean-field BSDEJs under quadratic-exponential growth conditions.

entries.title: Controlling Temporal Pseudo-Label Marginals for Stable Online Test-Time Adaptation
entries.summary: Continual Test-Time Adaptation (CTTA) methods update models online using a stream of unlabeled data to overcome distribution shifts encountered at test time. However, CTTA is often unstable, as it can reinforce biases in early predictions and increasingly predict only a few classes, resulting in drift or even collapse. In this paper, we identify narrowing pseudo-label class usage as an indicator of CTTA instability and quantify this behavior. Most existing methods have attempted to address this issue by either selecting reliable adaptation samples or re-weighting the loss to encourage diverse pseudo-labels, but they do not explicitly enforce a class marginal over a temporal window. Instead, we propose Sinkhorn Class-Marginal Regularization (SCALAR), a simple plug-and-play module that controls the pseudo-label distribution over a short temporal window. SCALAR works by maintaining recent predictions in a buffer, balancing their class distribution via the Sinkhorn algorithm to match a specified target distribution, and using the balanced soft targets for adaptation. Without changing the model architecture, SCALAR maintains the per-step runtime and increases the peak allocated GPU memory by only 10 MB on ImageNet-C. Our method is particularly effective on skewed, non-stationary data with severe distribution shifts, where SCALAR significantly alleviates drift and collapse when combined with existing stabilization methods based on entropy or diversity.
entries.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 20 pages. Code: https://github.com/r-isr/SCALAR

entries.title: The balance between feature learning and collapse in dynamical systems-based generative models
entries.summary: Over the past decade, a growing body of work has established that implicit biases in learning dynamics fundamentally shape the solutions found by neural networks, governing their learned features and generalisation performance. However, despite these strides in deep learning theory, far less is known about representation learning in generative models based on dynamical systems, from normalising flows to diffusion. Importantly, empirical evidence suggests that continuous-time generative models can be prone to mode collapse, yet a learning theory explaining such biases remains elusive. To address this, we use tools from dynamical systems and operator theory to express the gradient flow of a general class of stochastic differential equations as a composition of linear operators, allowing us to relate collapse to low-rank biases in generative models. In variational inference and flow-matching tasks, we show that this bias can manifest in two different mechanisms: i) where collapsed models are stable fixed points of the gradient flow, or ii) in sequential feature learning, where smaller modes take progressively longer to be learned, producing an effective collapse for a fixed training budget. Together these findings point to a trade-off between feature learning and collapse, suggesting an operator view as a step towards a unified framework for understanding the learning dynamics of dynamical systems-based generative models.

entries.title: Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey
entries.summary: Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schrödinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.

entries.title: BARS: Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis via Flow Matching
entries.summary: We present BARS (Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis), a non-autoregressive rapping voice generation model based on Flow Matching, conditioned on a beat track (instrumental backing), lyrics, and a short reference voice for zero-shot timbre control. Unlike prior autoregressive rap synthesis, where rap pace and output duration are strictly determined by the beat, BARS enables independent control over the rap tempo, allowing flexible-length generation without explicit duration prediction or phoneme-level alignment. We encode lyrics using a pretrained ByT5 encoder with a lightweight Transformer adapter trained jointly with the model, without relying on speech-pretrained text encoders, enabling natural handling of non-standard orthography (e.g., slang, abbreviations) and numerals common in rap lyrics. To address alignment instabilities, such as token skipping or repetition, under strong beat conditioning, we propose Asymmetric Scaled RoPE for cross-attention, which introduces a positional structure to facilitate sequential lyric-audio alignment learning. Furthermore, the model supports partial re-generation via span masking, enabling lyric-level editing while preserving the surrounding vocal style. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high lyric fidelity, natural rap flow that is rhythmically coherent with the beat, and robust tempo control across a wide range of rapping styles and speeds.
entries.comment: Published in ISMIR 2026 (Best Paper Award nominee). Demo: https://bars-ismir2026.github.io/bars/
entries.journalRef: Proceedings of the 27th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (ISMIR), 2026

entries.title: How Many Candidates Does a One-Step World Model Need? A Random-Codebook Account of Nearest-of-m Training on Frozen DINO Tokens
entries.summary: One-step stochastic world models avoid the mode averaging of deterministic feature predictors without the tens of network evaluations per step that diffusion and flow matching require. The simplest such objective is nearest-of-m matching (conditional implicit maximum likelihood estimation, IMLE): draw m candidate futures and pull only the one closest to the observed outcome. Recent work conjectures that a small m suffices for feature-space world models and that a strictly proper energy score should replace the hard minimum. We test both claims with one-step world models on frozen DINOv2/v3 patch tokens, using benchmarks whose futures can be enumerated. Under mode-like uncertainty, nearest-of-m with m=16 covers the enumerated futures better than 50-step flow matching (at about 1/30 of its latency), one-step flow generators and an energy-score generator at matched parameter counts, and its rollouts stay on the token manifold where flow rollouts drift. One quantity governs the choice of m: the nearest-of-m objective is the expected distortion of a random codebook of m draws from the generator. This view yields three predictions, recorded before the corresponding runs: (i) memorization of the realized outcome in contexts that never repeat, whose strength is governed by the codebook's miss distortion I(m) rather than its miss probability, and which an energy-score generator does not escape by raising m; (ii) a flattening of mode probabilities with m, matching a known optimum within 0.01; and (iii) under-dispersion on continuous high-dimensional outcomes, which bounds the method on real robot video. Per-step matching on self-rollouts cuts long-horizon error by a third on a stochastic Push-T variant; an ablation separates its manifold and coverage benefits. Planning success does not improve despite accurate risk estimates, a negative result we report with its diagnosis.
entries.comment: 30 pages (12-page main text, appendices A-H). Code: https://github.com/thddydgnl/nearest-of-m-world-models

entries.title: DeltaForge: A Post-hoc Mixture-of-Experts VLA for Multi-Domain Autonomous Driving
entries.summary: Fleets of driving vision-language-action (VLA) models are developed one domain at a time: each operator finetunes a shared base model on private data, producing specialized experts that are costly to consolidate into a single model. Weight merging loses accuracy as heterogeneous domains accumulate, and dense mixture-of-experts routing is prohibitively expensive to combine them. We present DeltaForge, to our knowledge the first post-hoc mixture-of-experts VLA for driving, which consolidates N independently finetuned per-domain models into a single multi-domain model from their weights and a small proxy set alone. When different operators finetune the same base model, their weight updates end up sharing a lot of structure. We exploit this by decomposing all the updates together using singular value decomposition (SVD), splitting each one into a shared part (the same across all domains) and a tiny domain-specific part. The router then only needs to work with those tiny domain-specific pieces, not the full expert weights, which is what keeps the approach efficient. Then two cooperating clip-level blind routers, one over the VLM reasoning experts and one over the flow-matching dynamics experts, are trained from soft labels on the proxy dataset. Across six diverse domains spanning urban, off-road, and highway driving on cars, trucks, and all-terrain vehicles (ATVs), DeltaForge approaches the accuracy of the per-domain experts and surpasses every merging, routing, centralized, and federated baseline at close to single-model parameter and compute cost. Adding a new domain requires only projecting its weight update onto the shared basis with no end-to-end retraining needed. The resulting model also generalizes to domain combinations it was never explicitly trained on.

entries.title: How Path Integral Diffusion Decides a Finite Spin Glass
entries.summary: When an AI diffusion-type generator samples a frustrated spin glass, which macroscopic alternatives does it decide first, and when? We study this for bridge-diffusion models of the Path Integral Diffusion (PID) type started from a point source. We show that every isotropic PID is a time-changed Gaussian stochastic localization, and conversely every signal-to-noise schedule is realized by a PID protocol. What a continuous-time generator decides therefore does not depend on the protocol, which only sets when and at what cost. We describe the generator's state by its partial commitments: the probabilities it assigns, at each moment, to nested classes of configurations fixed by the target. The partial commitments are martingales that move only along class contrasts. Their ensemble average gives the information about each level at an exact rate set by squared magnetization contrasts. Each split is decided, approximately, like a binary Gaussian channel at signal-to-noise ratio 1.04/λ_P, with λ_P the leading eigenvalue of the parent's correlation matrix. The theory is applied to Bethe-lattice and Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) glasses with up to 64 spins. It is observed generically that a trajectory first shifts its weight to one of the two mirror halves of the zero-field measure and then to the glassy classes inside it. These classes appear near the glass transition and keep their identity on cooling. Nested glassy levels have similar λ_P and are decided together, so a trajectory commits in one or two distinct events---the mirror choice and a compound glassy decision---which separate further with coupling and size, as the spectra predict. For a generator that takes finitely many steps, the protocol matters through the late, local stage rather than the macroscopic decisions.

entries.title: McKean--Vlasov Diffusions from Liouville Spectral Green Response
entries.summary: For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion with $0<γ<2$, the Gaussian response of a finite vector of logarithmic eigenvalues determines a conditional Green energy. We weight this energy by the current spectral density in the fixed reference space. The resulting self-consistent evolution is a porous-medium equation for the canonical spectral form. We construct its positive probability flow, prove an energy identity, and pass from the regularized response forms to the Green limit. The energy identity yields strong convergence of the Gaussian gradients and of the conditional response drifts. A superposition argument then realizes the flow as a McKean--Vlasov weak diffusion.

entries.title: Particle Filtering with Generative Trajectory Models for State Estimation and Control
entries.summary: Generative models can support both state estimation and control in robotics. For control, a common approach is to use the model as a policy that directly samples actions conditioned on observation histories. However, models that jointly represent states, actions, and observations can also predict how the robot state and its environment evolve. We investigate whether these predictions can improve state estimation and control through a change in inference procedure, without modifying the pretrained model. To this end, we use particle filtering to maintain competing hypotheses about state histories. A single pretrained diffusion model generates these hypotheses along with their predicted observations and associated action proposals. As new measurements arrive, particles are reweighted according to how well their predicted observations match the measurements. While particle filtering conventionally uses these weights only for state estimation, we also use them to guide action selection, favoring proposals associated with hypotheses that better explain the observations. Simulation experiments in partially observed navigation and vision-based manipulation demonstrate improvements in both state estimation and task performance compared to action generation without filtering, using the same pretrained model and no additional test-time information.

entries.title: A Sequential Monte Carlo Method for Data Assimilation in Subsurface Flow Systems with Hierarchical Uncertainty
entries.summary: Subsurface flow systems often involve hierarchical geological uncertainty, meaning both higher-level metaparameters and cell-by-cell properties are uncertain. This leads to challenges for data assimilation because both sets of parameters must be estimated. In this work we develop an adaptive-tempered sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) procedure for joint Bayesian estimation of these quantities. The method uses noncentered geological parameterizations, with geomodel realizations represented by metaparameters and Gaussian latent variables that are independent under the prior. Adaptive likelihood tempering, importance weighting, resampling, and blockwise Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) mutation are applied at each iteration. Flow surrogates are used for all function evaluations. The hierarchical SMC procedure is further extended to treat successive data assimilation. In this case, existing posterior particles are updated in a manner that accounts for correlations in surrogate model errors across observation batches. We consider two distinct 3D systems with hierarchical uncertainty. The first is a faulted carbon storage system containing three stacked aquifers and two extensive faults. Principal component analysis is used to represent target-aquifer heterogeneity, while geological metaparameters characterize uncertain aquifer and fault properties. The second is a channelized oil-water system containing three facies with uncertain properties. A latent diffusion model represents variability in channel geometry and facies realizations. For the four synthetic true models considered, SMC posterior metaparameter distributions and flow predictions agree closely with reference MCMC results. SMC, however, requires fewer function evaluations and provides speedups of 2.5--7.0 for single-stage data assimilation. Even greater speedups are achieved with multiple GPUs.

entries.title: Adjoint Kernel Sensitivity of the Rough Heston Characteristic Exponent
entries.summary: Multi-factor approximations of rough volatility kernels affect the characteristic exponents used in Fourier-based derivative valuation. We derive an adjoint representation for the first-order sensitivity of the rough Heston characteristic exponent with respect to its memory kernel, with model parameters and the input variance curve held fixed. The Volterra--Riccati functional $\mathcal L_T(K,z)$ admits a local real-analytic extension, jointly in the kernel perturbation and the transform parameter. The Fréchet derivative of this extension with respect to the kernel in $L^1$ is represented by integration against a continuous sensitivity kernel $B_K(u,z)$, obtained from a backward linear Volterra equation and independent of the perturbation direction. This representation resolves the leading-order contributions of kernel perturbations across memory lags. On the structural kernel class, which contains the fractional kernel and its multi-factor approximations and has empty interior in $L^1$, the extension yields Hadamard directional differentiability and a first-order expansion with a quadratic $L^1$-remainder for all sufficiently close structural kernels, uniformly on compact subsets of the strip of transform parameters. The same sensitivity kernel yields multi-factor weight and decay-rate derivatives. Numerical experiments at multi-factor reference kernels assess the finite-resolution implementation and illustrate how the lag distribution of positive perturbations with equal $L^1$ mass affects the first-order response.

entries.title: GenISys: Integrated Ship Systems Design Using Subsystem-Conditional Tabular Diffussion
entries.summary: Ship design requires coordinating coupled subsystems to satisfy engineering constraints and balance competing performance and cost objectives. Generative artificial intelligence has supported component design, but integrated ship generation must also account for interactions among hull geometry, structure, propulsion, and operation. This paper presents GenISys, a framework for generating integrated systems, demonstrated through early-stage bulk-carrier design. Its dataset contains 217,999 proposed designs, including 16,247 that satisfy the formulated engineering constraints. The proposed simultaneous conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (SCDDPM) generates subsystems together, allowing each subsystem model to respond to changes elsewhere during generation. Experiments compare this approach with monolithic whole-ship generation and sequential subsystem generation across five independent training runs per architecture. In a study targeting lower cost per tonne of cargo transported, designs were generated for a required voyage range of 5,000 nautical miles. SCDDPM produced designs satisfying the formulated engineering constraints and meeting a common low-cost target in 55.70% of generation requests, compared with 51.10% for the monolithic model and 47.54% for the sequential model. These correspond to 9.0% and 17.2% more qualifying designs, respectively, while maintaining similar estimated transport costs. These results show how generative artificial intelligence can coordinate subsystems to generate feasible, high-performing integrated systems.

entries.title: The Shape of a Program: Path Signatures for Trace-to-Program Induction
entries.summary: Synthesizing programs from execution traces is a fundamental challenge in algorithmic interpretability and the reverse engineering of complex systems. We bring a rough-path-theoretic perspective to program induction, treating execution traces as high-dimensional rough paths and encoding them with the path signature transform, a tool from stochastic analysis whose expectation provably characterizes the distribution of traces a program induces. On three program-induction domains, Karel, List, and RASP, our log-signature trace encoder outperforms LSTM, Transformer, and Fourier baselines in almost every setting, with its largest margins when training data is scarce. We further observe that the trace-to-program pipeline is naturally contractive: it often produces valid programs that are shorter than the ground truth. We turn this into a bootstrapping procedure that exposes redundancy in the ground-truth supervision without any external oracle, which we demonstrate on redundancy-injected versions of our datasets. Finally, the log-signature encoder induces a markedly more interpretable latent geometry than the baselines, in which the nearest neighbors of every state lie on its own execution trace.

entries.title: When Should Diffusion Language Models Reconsider Their Commitments?
entries.summary: Masked Diffusion Models (MDMs) are well known for fast text generation via parallel decoding. However, independent parallel sampling can commit to inconsistent predictions, and less is known about how to selectively revise these early token commitments. In this work, we introduce $\underline{\mathrm{P}}$lanned $\underline{\mathrm{U}}$nmasking-and-$\underline{\mathrm{R}}$evision Joint $\underline{\mathrm{L}}$earning (PURL) for MDMs, a training-based framework that seamlessly unifies parallel generation with selective token revision. We derive a normalized joint transition whose likelihood factorizes into edit selection, unmask selection, and token prediction. These components are trained jointly on partially masked sequences constructed according to the model's own unmasking policy. During inference, all three decisions are supported by a single shared forward pass, enabling the model to decode masked tokens and revise noisy tokens. Across logic puzzles, mathematical reasoning, and code generation, PURL improves accuracy at matched unmask budgets, with relative gains up to 47.4% accuracy improvement and up to an $8\times$ reduction in scheduled decoding rounds. Beyond these gains, our analysis further reveals general principles of revisable decoding: token edits become more effective as context accumulates; early edits can steer unfinished trajectories, whereas later edits tend to remain localized; and effective edits therefore depend on both calibrating when to intervene and learning where and how to revise. Together, these suggest that effective parallel generation depends not on revising more tokens, but on making the right commitments revisable at the right time.

entries.title: Music Inpainting With Similarity-Guided Latent Diffusion
entries.summary: We propose a music inpainting technique combining similarity matching and a diffusion-based generative model to replace large segments of audio recordings with suitable alternatives. The proposed hybrid method, Similarity-Guided Diffusion Posterior Sampling (SimDPS), retrieves candidate replacement segments from the wider signal based on contextual similarity and uses them to guide the diffusion process toward coherent reconstructions. Being model-agnostic, the framework is compatible with any pre-trained diffusion model operating in either the waveform or latent domain. Objective evaluations demonstrate that SimDPS outperforms widely adopted RePaint and DPS methods across acoustic features and neural-embedding distance metrics. Subjective evaluations on multi-genre music datasets confirm that SimDPS enhances perceptual plausibility compared to previous diffusion-based methods and demonstrates robustness to poorly matched similarity candidates. These findings pave the way for improved music restoration and context-aware audio editing.
entries.comment: Accepted to ISMIR 2026. 8 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Code and audio examples: https://s-turland.github.io/SimDPSInpainting/

entries.title: InfCoiL: Coordinated Planner-Controller Learning for Closed-Loop Physics-Based Human-Object Interaction
entries.summary: Text- and goal-conditioned human-object interaction (HOI) provides an intuitive interface for specifying high-level intents in physics-based character animation. Mapping such intents to physically plausible, contact-rich behaviors naturally calls for a generative planner and a physics-based controller, yet existing planner-controller systems either execute plans open-loop or close the loop while keeping the planner fixed, so execution feedback never reshapes what is planned. We present InfCoiL, a closed-loop framework for physics-based HOI from coordinated planner-controller learning. InfCoiL couples a morphology-aware flow-matching planner with a unified multi-morphology controller through a shared morphology interface in an autoregressive plan-and-execute loop, and alternately fine-tunes both components with reinforcement learning from the same physical rollouts. To optimize the flow-matching planner online, we introduce Semantic Flow Policy Optimization (SFPO), which stochasticizes selected denoising transitions with channel-wise semantic covariance over heterogeneous HOI features and assigns group-relative, sequence-level rewards from complete closed-loop executions. On held-out OMOMO sequences, InfCoiL outperforms open-loop hierarchical baselines in goal-reaching task success and physical tracking accuracy. Project page: https://infcoil.github.io/

entries.title: Identifiable alignment of unpaired representations
entries.summary: Aligning two models without paired data requires a distance that both share, yet existing methods use Euclidean or spherical geometry. This is either an arbitrary choice or imposed by their loss function. We show that, under a precise form of the manifold hypothesis, the pullback of the data metric gives such a distance for any two models of one data-generating process. This holds whether the models are encoders, decoders or both, and whatever their architecture, loss, prior or training data. The alignment map preserves this distance and the distribution of representations, and is identifiable if and only if the data distribution breaks every symmetry of the data manifold. We show that this symmetry breaking holds generically. Identifiability makes the alignment coupling the unique optimum of Gromov--Wasserstein and of its weighted combinations with a linear program. The linear program alone has the same optimum if almost every data point has a distinct distribution of distances. The coupling, and with it the alignment map, is recovered exactly from permuted samples, even without identifiability, and consistently from independent ones. Our method, Neural Gromov--Monge Alignment (NGMA), uses no pairs or labels and outperforms every unpaired and label-informed baseline. It relies on pullback distances to align image models with different priors and single-cell models trained on disjoint cells, where Euclidean distances fail.
entries.comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

entries.title: Retrospective Analysis of Team-Following Trading Profitability in Pumpfun Meme Coins Using Funding Networks
entries.summary: If the right token-creation teams had been known, how much could following them have returned, and what is left when only information available before each launch is used? We study ten separately recorded Pumpfun windows (April 2024 to September 2026), each reconstructed independently from real-SOL reserve states and finite-capital accounts that start with one SOL. Teams are directed funding groups ranked in hindsight. When every team exits at its own best reserve threshold, chosen in hindsight, the main account ends above one SOL in all 8 windows that have a qualifying team (1.10 to 11.32 SOL), but free cash exceeds one SOL in only 5, and marks of positions that never reached their threshold make up 17--94% of equity. If teams are recognised online, from tokens whose first hour has completed, 9 of 19 teams become identifiable only after their last launch; the remaining 10 end above one SOL in 10 cases, with free cash above one SOL in 7; funding links in this step still come from the full window, so even these results are not a fully realisable signal. A large model balance, a result above random cohorts that repeat the threshold search, and a statistical rejection in the selection-matched nulls (3 of 40 tests after Holm adjustment) are three different statements, and these nulls condition on the discovered funding graph, so they do not calibrate the whole selection procedure. Midpoint tests describe a further source of apparent opportunity. A detailed analysis of the best and the worst window, with every analysis parameter varied, shows that the worst result, which is close to break-even, rises several-fold with a stop rule or another funding-graph construction. The results are conditional retrospective model accounts, not executable profits, and not evidence of a causal effect of the SOL price.

entries.title: Flex-DDCM: Zero-Shot Task-Oriented Image Compression via Diffusion Trajectory Guidance
entries.summary: Recent zero-shot image compression methods exploit the powerful priors of pretrained diffusion models to produce perceptually pleasing reconstructions without compression-specific training. However, image compression serves not only human viewing but also machine analysis, while existing zero-shot codecs have limited flexibility in meeting the diverse reconstruction requirements of these applications. In this paper, we propose Flex-DDCM, a framework for zero-shot task-oriented image compression via diffusion trajectory guidance. Building on Turbo-DDCM, we adapt the coded diffusion trajectory through task-guided noise selection, embedding the effects of task guidance into the compressed representation. Guidance terms can be applied individually or combined, with timestep-dependent strengths controlling their influence throughout denoising. This design enables task adaptation without introducing additional decoding complexity. Experiments demonstrate flexible trade-offs among pixel fidelity, perceptual quality, and downstream task performance, with competitive performance against trained task-oriented codecs and faster decoding than Diff-ICMH.

entries.title: Fourth-Moment Theorems for Sums of Multiple Wigner Integrals
entries.summary: We derive quantitative free fourth-moment bounds for sums of two Wigner chaoses of opposite parity under mirror symmetry. The bound contains an explicit remainder consisting of internal contractions of the two kernels. In particular, vanishing of this remainder together with the fourth free cumulant implies convergence to the standard semicircular law. If the higher-order kernel is cyclically symmetric, the internal contractions can be moved to an endpoint and we obtain an explicit fourth-root bound without a remainder. For fully symmetric kernels we obtain a square-root bound under the $W_2$-Wasserstein distance. Using the operator-norm support estimate for Wigner integrals, we also extend these bounds to every $W_p$-Wasserstein distance , where $1\le p<\infty$.

entries.title: Rate of convergence for the Wiener--Itô chaos in $W_p$ for $1\leq p<\infty$
entries.summary: Inspired by previous work of Nualart, Ledoux, Peccati, Nourdin, and others, we establish quantitative fourth moment theorems for random variables in a fixed Wiener--Itô chaos and for sums of two Wiener--Itô chaoses in the $W_p$-Wasserstein distance for $1\leq p<\infty$.

entries.title: Self-Supervised Collapse Prevention with Score-Based Entropy Maximization
entries.summary: Diffusion models have demonstrated the effectiveness of score-based objectives for generative modeling, yet their potential for self-supervised representation learning remains underexplored. We introduce Entropy-Based Regularization (EBReg), a framework that uses latent score estimation to regularize the latent distribution during self-supervised training. EBReg jointly learns an encoder and a latent score model, and utilizes the learned score to provide a diversity-preserving signal that prevents representational collapse. Motivated by a mutual-information lower bound, we formulate the objective as view alignment with smoothed marginal entropy maximization and optimize the marginal entropy without explicit density evaluation. The same score model can additionally be used at test time to refine corrupted representations toward the training latent distribution. Empirically, EBReg learns competitive representations on ImageNet-1K, achieving 75.57% linear-probe accuracy with ViT-L. Across diverse architectures, score-guided test-time adaptation further improves robustness on ImageNet-C, yielding an average relative accuracy gain of approximately 5%.

entries.title: Discrete Diffusion Playground: A 2D Benchmark for Discrete Generative Models
entries.summary: Discrete diffusion is a promising framework for categorical generative modeling, but current evaluation protocols often fail to reveal whether models have actually learned the target distribution. We introduce the Discrete Diffusion Playground, a diagnostic benchmark that converts known 2D continuous distributions into binary token sequences through an exact discretized bijection. This creates a rare setting in which models are trained on discrete sequences, but generated samples can be decoded back into 2D and compared directly against a known ground-truth distribution. The benchmark spans smooth Gaussian mixtures and tilted checkerboards with sharp boundaries, disconnected support, and coordinate-dependent structure, allowing it to expose failures that are invisible in standard proxy metrics. It supports exact grid divergences, Wasserstein distances, density visualizations, and nonparametric two-sample tests, providing both quantitative evaluation and interpretable failure diagnosis. Using this testbed, we show that masked diffusion models can learn meaningful adaptive reveal orders but remain less stable than autoregressive baselines on smooth targets and largely fail on tilted checkerboards, where autoregressive models preserve the target geometry. Control experiments with reversed and interleaved token orderings show that autoregressive performance is not explained by favorable bit order alone. The Playground provides a simple but stringent benchmark for stress-testing discrete generative models and for developing evaluation metrics that detect real distributional mismatch rather than proxy performance. Our code is available at https://github.com/shaojus/DiscreteDiffusionPlayground .
entries.comment: 18 pages, 7 main figures, 2 tables. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations and Datasets Track)

entries.title: DPDP: Diffusion Policy-Steered Diffusion Planner for Offline Reinforcement Learning
entries.summary: In offline reinforcement learning, diffusion models fill two roles with complementary strengths. Typically guided by a critic, a diffusion policy is value-aware and favors high-return, behavior-supported actions, but it is short-sighted: it never lays out the states it intends to visit. A diffusion planner is far-sighted, synthesizing such a long-horizon trajectory, but it is only behavior-driven at execution, realizing each planned transition using only offline behavior.Each is strong exactly where the other is weak. We introduce DPDP to bring them together at the planner's execution step, where a planned transition becomes an action. Reading the planner's inverse-dynamics executor as a posterior over actions: the environment's transition likelihood relates an action to the planned next state, while the behavioral prior determines its weight under the offline data. Replacing this prior with a value-optimized diffusion policy preserves the planned transition likelihood and favors valuable actions that can serve the plan. We target the resulting clean-action distribution in two ways. A training-free sampler composes policy and inverse-dynamics scores at matched action noise levels and applies Langevin correction; this route uses a shared action noise schedule and an approximately common terminal prior. A preference objective instead amortizes the transfer into a single diffusion executor. Across D4RL, DPDP improves the planner it builds on, staying competitive with reactive diffusion policies on locomotion and leading on long-horizon navigation.

entries.title: An Analysis of Reinforcement Learning with Function Approximation
entries.summary: We address the problem of computing the optimal Q-function in Markov decision problems with infinite state-space. We analyze the convergence properties of several variations of Q-learning when combined with function approximation, extending the analysis of TD-learning in Tsitsiklis and Van Roy (1996) to stochastic control settings. We identify conditions under which such approximate methods converge with probability 1. We conclude with a brief discussion on the general applicability of our results and compare them with several related works.
entries.comment: This version of the paper corrects the one that was presented at the 25th International Conference on Machine Learning. entries.title: Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning for an Options Market Maker: An Empirical Study with Real S&P 500 Options
entries.summary: Options market makers absorb client order flow and must hedge the resulting inventory risk under trading frictions. We study whether an option hedging reinforcement learning (RL) agent trained on historical market data outperforms three alternatives in tail-risk protection: (i) traditional delta hedging, (ii) simple hedge-ratio rules, and (iii) the same agent trained in simulated markets. Most RL hedging agents are trained in model-generated markets that do not capture the crashes and volatility regimes present in real data. We introduce an empirical replay environment using S&P 500 option data from 1996 to 2017 and compare against a matched geometric Brownian motion (GBM) environment, a stochastic-volatility (SABR) simulator, and a hybrid that values historical paths with Black-Scholes, all sharing the same portfolio mechanics, stochastic arrivals, costs, and test period. We train a distributional Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) agent and evaluate it out of sample over 2018-2023. The agent trained on empirical data reduces Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) tail loss by 3.1% compared to delta hedging and outperforms every hedge-ratio rule chosen during the training period and every alternative training environment. The reduction reaches 8.9% in volatile and falling markets, but reverses to a cost of 7-10% in rising markets. Empirical training induces a state-dependent short net delta: the policy under-hedges negative-delta books, most strongly after prices have fallen. This tilt disappears with GBM training and is weaker with SABR or hybrid training. These findings suggest that exposure to historical market dynamics can materially change a tail-risk hedging policy, although the evidence rests on a single test path and the edge is regime-conditional.
entries.comment: 9 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables. Authors listed alphabetically by last name

entries.title: An Introduction to Applied Probability and Stochastic Processes: Open Lecture Notes
entries.summary: These open lecture notes provide a broad introduction to measure-theoretic probability and stochastic processes, with a focus on applications. Topics include probability spaces, conditional expectation, generating and characteristic functions, Markov chains in discrete and continuous time, convergence of random variables, Brownian motion, stochastic calculus, stochastic differential equations and their connection to partial differential equations, jump diffusions, stochastic control, optimal stopping, and Monte Carlo methods. Most chapters include exercises, and solutions are provided. The notes were written for a two-quarter course for first-year PhD students in applied mathematics, and should also be useful to graduate students in statistics, engineering, economics and finance. The LaTeX source is freely available on GitHub under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license, and readers are encouraged to fork the notes and contribute corrections, improvements, and new material.
entries.comment: Lecture notes, approx. 320 pages. LaTeX source: https://github.com/mattlorig/intro-probability-stochastic-processes

entries.title: CoupledFlow: One-Step Neural Operators for Coupled Multi-Physics PDEs
entries.summary: This paper introduces COUPLED FLOW, a new neural operator learning framework for multi-physics PDE systems that captures the co-evolution of multiple physical processes by modeling their cross-process interactions. Unlike existing neural operator methods that primarily target single-physics settings, COUPLED FLOW employs a novel structure-constrained flow matching algorithm to learn process- specific mean velocity fields conditioned on the full multi-physics state. This enables fast and accurate one-step prediction of coupled PDE systems that would otherwise require expensive numerical simulations. A key challenge in training COUPLED FLOW however lies in sampling structure-constrained conditional flow interpolants that capture cross-process correlations and serve as training examples for flow matching. To address this challenge, we derive a multi-physics mean-flow consistency identity that characterizes cross-process interactions and defines the structure-constrained mean-flow matching loss. To provide informative training samples for flow matching with this loss, we develop a principled method for sampling correlated conditional interpolants based on posterior multi-output Gaus- sian processes, which capture richer cross-process correlations than the commonly used endpoint-conditioned linear interpolants. We also establish a theoretical re- sult showing that the Wasserstein-2 distance between the predicted and oracle PDE solution distributions is upper-bounded in terms of the structure-constrained flow matching loss and the smoothness of the learned flow. Experiments across diverse coupled PDE benchmarks demonstrate that COUPLED FLOW consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art neural operators and generative PDE solvers.

entries.title: Polynomial-Preserving Processes and Volatility Modelling in Discrete Time
entries.summary: This paper develops a discrete-time framework for volatility modelling and derivative pricing based on polynomial preservation. The framework provides exact moments of arbitrary order and serial cross-moments of variance and return processes over any finite horizon through finite-dimensional matrix representations. This analytical tractability is maintained while accommodating flexible leverage and variance-of-variance dynamics and non-Gaussian innovations. We introduce two novel classes of stochastic volatility models that nest widely used discrete-time specifications and study their statistical properties. Under two distinct scaling regimes, we establish weak convergence to polynomial diffusions and jump-diffusions and convergence of polynomial moments, linking discrete-time moment recursions to continuous-time matrix-exponential formulas. An empirical analysis of S\&P~500 returns and a large panel of options spanning 1996--2023 shows that the proposed specifications improve return fit and reduce mean weekly implied volatility root mean squared errors by approximately 8--41\% relative to their nested benchmarks, depending on the variance dynamics and innovation distribution.

entries.title: Prescriptive Learning of Linear Policies with Feasibility Guarantees for Binary Decision-Making
entries.summary: Binary decision-making under uncertainty arises across a wide range of applications, including energy systems scheduling, transportation, and workforce planning. While machine learning has been increasingly applied to accelerate or replace mixed-integer solvers in such settings, existing approaches rely on predictive learning, training models to reproduce optimal decisions from labeled data, which lacks knowledge of counterfactual outcomes and provides no guarantees that the resulting decisions will be feasible. This limitation is further compounded under distributional shift, where policies trained on historical data may produce systematically infeasible decisions. We propose a prescriptive learning framework for binary decision-making that addresses both limitations. Rather than predicting optimal labels, the framework jointly optimizes over linear decision policies and feasible assignments across all training scenarios, allowing feasible alternatives and their operational performance to be considered directly during training. We further extend the framework to a distributionally robust chance-constrained formulation using a Wasserstein ambiguity set, which enforces feasibility with a prescribed probability under the worst-case distribution in the ambiguity set and enables a tunable trade-off between robustness and solution quality. We demonstrate the framework on two case studies, namely a unit commitment problem and a staff allocation problem. Out-of-sample experiments under test distributions that either match or differ from the training distribution show that the robust model is more conservative when the two distributions coincide, while under distributional shift it substantially reduces unmet demand and lowers total cost by up to 76.5% relative to classical predictive learning.

entries.title: Zero-Shot VLA Adaptation with Retrieved Guidance
entries.summary: Pre-training large parametric "Vision-Language-Action" (VLA) models on large demonstration datasets has recently yielded promising results for general-purpose manipulation. However, these models still struggle under even small domain shifts relative to the training data, such as changes in camera viewpoint, background, object identity, or robot morphology. Motivated by the success of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in language models, we pursue retrieval to boost VLA performance. Specifically, we seek to leverage retrieval from domain-mismatched, "in-the-wild" demonstration datasets like DROID to guide a VLA's behavior in a new target domain. To achieve this, we introduce RAGu, which overcomes robotics-specific challenges for RAG: (1) It incorporates simple geometric calibration to transform source demonstrations into the target setup and reduce cross-domain differences. (2) It uses a coarse-to-fine retrieval strategy that selects, from a large pool of pre-warped candidates, the trajectory most compatible with the base VLA. (3) It guides the VLA's flow-matching inference procedure rather than seeking to retrain the base model or expand its limited context window. We evaluate RAGu across real-world, simulation, sim-to-real transfer, and cross-embodiment humanoid manipulation. We find it improves real-world VLA success rates from 20% to 80% and outperforms the closest-related baselines in sim. Project website: raguvla.github.io

entries.title: Guiding future global temperature distributions with simulations and observations
entries.summary: Assessing climate risks requires projections of daily temperature distributions, including rare and spatially widespread extremes. Climate simulations are costly and biased, while correcting them toward observations risks suppressing inter-model differences. We train a single machine-learning emulator, a conditional diffusion model, on seventeen CMIP6 models and ERA5 reanalysis to generate spatially coherent daily temperature fields conditioned on model identity, date, and CO2-equivalent concentration. At sampling time, diffusion guidance reduces model biases by steering each emulated climate-model distribution toward observations, with its strength selected through perfect-model experiments using withheld simulated futures. Observational influence decreases with projection horizon and forcing. Across seventeen synthetic targets, guidance more than halves median biases in the 1st and 99th percentiles of daily temperature, improves probabilistic scores and reliability, and reduces median annual global-mean temperature RMSE by 32-57% across three emission scenarios. In a detailed benchmark, guidance also outperforms established bias corrections on daily-field probabilistic scores. Efficient sampling generates large ensembles without further climate simulations. For example, our framework corrects CMIP6's roughly threefold historical overestimate of extreme-heat coverage, yet projects that concurrent extremes will affect nearly half of global land on a typical day in the 2080s under SSP3-7.0.
